manifest.name: dsh-native-memory
manifest.description: Native, per-workspace long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness: facts and profiles on DSH's own storage-domain, cross-session recall through session-query FTS, approval-gated writes, and cited provenance — no external server, no extra runtime dependency.

bundle.text:
# dsh-native-memory bundle patch.
#
# Applied as one layer after the profile's shipped bundles (dsh-base and the
# mode bundle) and before the user's own profile cordis.patch.yml — the user's
# layer wins. Two changes:
#
#   1. session-query-sqlite config override: enable full-text search so
#      cross-session recall works. The shipped default is `openAt: never`
#      (search calls fail with SESSION_QUERY_SEARCH_DISABLED); `first-search`
#      defers the node:sqlite import and index open to the first search call.
#      The durable index lives next to the other storage units.
#
#   2. One host-plane plugin row: the memory service. Memory is a
#      cross-session capability, so its row belongs to the HOST composition
#      (plane rule: anything crossing sessions stays host-side), never loose
#      inside an agent preset. It publishes no service — it consumes the
#      host's registries — so it needs no isolate realm.
#
# Config note: a patch REPLACES a targeted row's whole `config` rather than
# merging into it. Any field the deployment customized on
# `session-query-sqlite` is therefore overridden here and must be restated
# in the user's own cordis.patch.yml, which always applies last.

- id: session-query-sqlite
  config:
    path: !!js dshHomePath('storages/session-search.sqlite')
    openAt: first-search

- insert:
    - id: dsh-native-memory
      name: 'dsh-native-memory'
      config:
        # Bounded workspace profile injected into the system prompt of every
        # session (order 88, before tool guidance). Disable here or in a
        # later patch layer when prompt overhead matters more than recall.
        injectProfile: true
        # Durable facts per workspace. Hard caps keep recall deterministic
        # and the always-on profile bounded.
        maxFactsPerWorkspace: 300
        maxFactChars: 2000
        # The always-injected workspace profile: few, dense entries.
        maxProfileEntries: 8
        maxProfileEntryChars: 240
        # Write tools (remember / edit / forget) pass the host approval
        # stack; every ask/outcome pair lands on the requesting session log.
        approvalWrites: true
        # Writes reject secret-shaped text (tokens / keys / passwords).
        # 'mask' stores them masked; 'off' stores as-is (injection always masks).
        secretPolicy: reject
        # Session-end memory proposal (OFF by default): the LLM distills the
        # finished session into candidate facts shown in the NEXT sessions'
        # prompt; they become facts only through the approval-gated
        # memory_remember. The LLM proposes, the human approves.
        proposeOnSessionEnd: false
        proposalProvider: deepseek
        proposalModel: deepseek-v4-flash
        proposalMaxFacts: 8
        proposalMaxPending: 16
        proposalTtlDays: 7
        # Compaction drift guard (ON): anchors a summary dropped surface as
        # DATA to verify in the next sessions' prompt. Deterministic, no LLM.
        compactionGuard: true
        guardAlarmTtlHours: 24
        guardAlarmMax: 3

readme.text:
[](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) [](LICENSE)

Native, per-workspace long-term memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`): facts and profiles stored on the harness's **own** storage-domain, cross-session recall through **session-query FTS**, **approval-gated** writes, and cited provenance — no external server, no extra runtime dependency.

> ⚠️ Installing a plugin runs third-party code on your machine with your own
> permissions. Review the source ([`src/`](src)) and [the security model](docs/security.md)
> before installing.

| | dsh-hermes-memory | dsh-native-memory |
|---|---|---|
| Storage | `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` namespace | dedicated storage-domain unit (`~/.dsh/storages/dsh_memory.json`) |
| Scope | user-global, all projects | **per workspace** (exact-cwd authorization) |
| Write safety | silent, model-only | **human approval gate** + session-log audit |
| Recall | everything always injected (hard caps) | bounded always-on profile **plus** on-demand recall + FTS over past sessions |
| Dependencies | vendored imports into the harness checkout | none beyond zod + the harness itself |

See [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) for the full architecture and the
competitive landscape analysis.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-native-memory   # npm after release
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/this/repo  # from a checkout
```

Restart `dsh web`. The bundle enables session-query full-text search and adds
the memory tools to every session. Details and configuration:
[docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

| Tool | Kind | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| `memory_remember` | add/update a fact in this workspace (secrets rejected by default) | approval |
| `memory_edit` | replace a fact | approval |
| `memory_forget` | archive a fact (soft delete) | approval |
| `memory_recall` | deterministic three-tier keyword scan (tags > text > fuzzy; freshness/access tie-breaks) | none |
| `memory_search` | FTS over this workspace's past sessions (caller excluded) | none |
| `memory_expand` | expand a fact's citation to the original log excerpt | none |
| `memory_consolidate` | near-duplicate merge suggestions + cap budget | none |
| `memory_import` | import candidate facts from a past session's log | approval (per fact) |
| `memory_profile` | read the always-injected workspace profile | none |
| `memory_export` | write a git-friendly Markdown mirror (`.dsh-memory/memory.md`, masked, idempotent) | none |

Every fact records its origin `(sessionId, seq)` — memory stays
reconstructable from the lossless session log.

Writes reject secret-shaped text (tokens / keys / passwords) by default;
`secretPolicy: "mask" | "off"` in the bundle patch relaxes that. The
credential-assignment detector can flag benign `token: …` values of ≥16
characters. Prompt injection and tool output always mask secrets.

A read-only browser page (settings → 记忆) lists every workspace's facts with
secrets masked; deletions are copied as a `memory_forget` instruction and land
in the chat through the approval gate.

Opt-in session-end proposals (`proposeOnSessionEnd: true`): one cheap LLM call
distills a finished session into candidate facts shown in the next sessions;
they become facts only through the approval-gated `memory_remember`.

A compaction drift guard (`compactionGuard: true`, on by default) surfaces
literal anchors a compaction summary dropped, as data to verify in the next
sessions — deterministic, no LLM.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test
```
